archetype.name: Gunslinger (pocket-bound)
archetype.definition: A rhythm pocket thrower who wins with accuracy and intermediate aggression, rarely runs, and has always paid for his big-play rate with more interceptions than most starters.

report.headline: Efficient arm, ugly EPA: interceptions and third downs hide a sound passer
report.take:
Darnold's 2026 is effectively two full games. He played 10% of snaps in Week 1, has no Week 2 line, then played every snap against Washington and the Chargers. The team's start log even credits Drew Lock with Weeks 2-4, so the record is muddy. What he has put on tape matches the passer of his last two seasons. He's accurate (the lowest bad-throw rate among qualifiers at 2.9%), he generates yardage (8.12 YPA, 6th), and he works the intermediate zone. Rushing adds nothing: 11 yards on four carries.

The gap between 8.12 YPA and a -0.043 EPA per dropback (27th) comes from three places. The first is turnovers: a 4.3% interception rate. The second is third down, where he has converted 22% at an average of 8.4 yards to go. The third is one-score football, where he sits at -0.306 EPA with all three interceptions and all four sacks. The Washington game was the swing. He threw for 379 yards and 4 TDs, but some of it came in a comeback: he went 10-for-10 when trailing by nine or more. He also threw two interceptions in a loss as an 8.5-point favorite. Against the Chargers he threw only 22 times, took three sacks and finished at -5.2 passing EPA despite two touchdowns.

Two stylistic shifts stand out. His time to throw is 3.31 seconds, against 2.87 last year. His aggressiveness, the share of throws into tight windows, is 22.4%, against 13.2%. He is holding the ball and squeezing it, which fits the intermediate production (+0.558 EPA, 73.7% completions, +14.4 CPOE) and the turnovers alike. The strangest number is the short game: 56% completions and -7.6 CPOE on throws of 0-9 air yards. That's almost certainly not an accuracy problem from a passer with his bad-throw rate. It looks receiver-driven. AJ Barner (-0.78 EPA per target on 12 targets) and Rashid Shaheed (-0.54 on 7) have given back value, while Jaxon Smith-Njigba (+0.37 on 21) and Cooper Kupp (+0.56) have produced.

The context around him is run-heavy and short of backs. Seattle passes 5.1 points less than expected (25th) despite a run game that ranks 26th in EPA. Jadarian Price is now on IR, and Zach Charbonnet hasn't been activated. If game scripts or the depleted backfield push the offense toward the pass, the underlying passer should look a lot more like the 2025 version (+0.162 EPA per play). The interceptions, though, are career-long and not a fluke.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy and aggression
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards have been his engine: +0.558 EPA, 74% success and 14.4 points of CPOE. That fits his jump in tight-window throws. The sample is only 19 attempts. Still, his 2024-25 YPA ranks (10th, 5th) say the downfield efficiency is real rather than a hot streak.

strengths.title: Ball placement is clean
strengths.body: Charting has him at the lowest bad-throw rate among qualifiers, and NGS puts his CPOE at +6.5. That fits a passer who has been above expectation for completions three straight healthy seasons. Misses on short throws look like receiver results, not an accuracy decline.

strengths.title: Pressure rarely becomes sacks
strengths.body: Only 6.7% of his pressures have turned into sacks, 2nd best. That's notable because he is holding the ball 3.31 seconds. His career pressure-to-sack rates have been middling, so expect some drift. The three sacks against the Chargers were more about a line that allows a high hit rate than about him freezing.

concerns.title: Interceptions are who he is
concerns.body: A 4.3% interception rate (37th of 42) is inflated by a tiny sample. But the trait isn't new: he ranked 53rd of 63 in interceptions in 2024 and 63rd of 65 in 2025. The rise in tight-window throws makes this the cost of his aggression rather than bad luck. Expect the rate to fall toward his recent norm, not disappear.

concerns.title: Third downs and one-score games
concerns.body: He has converted 22% of third downs at -0.457 EPA, and in one-score states he's at -0.306 with every sack and interception. That's where his EPA collapses. Long distances (8.4 average to go) behind a 26th-ranked run game make it harder. On 18 plays this is more likely to improve than define him.

concerns.title: Short game bleeding value
concerns.body: Throws of 0-9 air yards sit at -0.286 EPA with -7.6 CPOE, the opposite of how quick game normally works. Much of it traces to his tight end and secondary receivers. If the short game doesn't stabilize, he lacks easy completions to sustain drives.

trend.note: A 10%-snap Week 1 and no Week 2 line were followed by a 379-yard, four-TD, two-INT shootout and then a 22-attempt, three-sack grind. Two full games say little about direction, only that his range is wide.

nextGame.headline: Bosa-less 49ers front offers clean pockets, not cheap explosives
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's defense is middling against the pass (18th in pass EPA) and among the weakest at getting home: 27th in hit rate and 26th in sack rate. For a passer holding the ball 3.3 seconds, that matters. What the 49ers do well is cap big plays: they rank 2nd in explosive pass rate allowed and 4th in deep EPA. They give up underneath (23rd in short EPA), which is exactly where Darnold has struggled this year. The game script should also call for passing. The 49ers' offense leads the league in EPA and passing EPA. The 47.5 total is higher than any of Seattle's first three, and Seattle's defense is soft underneath (28th in short EPA).

Availability tilts toward Seattle's passing game. Nick Bosa is out and DT James Thompson Jr. is out, gutting a rush that was already weak. Safety Marques Sigle, an 88%-snap starter, is doubtful with a high-ankle sprain expected to cost multiple weeks, which loosens the back end over the middle. On Seattle's side, Jadarian Price is on IR and Zach Charbonnet won't be activated, leaving a thin backfield behind a run game already 26th in EPA. That pushes more of the offense onto Darnold, for better and worse.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pocket without Bosa
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers are already 26th in sack rate and 27th in hit rate, and they lose their top edge rusher and a DT. Darnold has been at his best when he has time to work the intermediate zone. This is a one-week edge tied to the injury list.

keyMatchups.title: Underneath space vs. his short struggles
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco concedes efficiency on short throws but rarely allows explosives. This game will test whether Darnold's 0-9 yard problem is a fluke. If the quick game finally connects, the drives sustain. If not, he'll be forced into tight intermediate windows against a defense built to limit them.

keyMatchups.title: Shootout pressure from SF's offense
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers' offense leads the league in passing EPA and allows the fewest hits, against a Seattle defense that ranks 28th on short throws. If San Francisco scores, Seattle's run-leaning script breaks and Darnold's volume climbs, as it did in the Washington game.

nextGame.watch: Whether the short passing game to Barner and the backs starts converting. That decides if this is a 270-yard day or another drive-stalling, interception-risk afternoon.

restOfSeason.body:
The skills that held up in 2024 and 2025 are all present: above-expected completion rate, top-tier ball placement and real intermediate efficiency. His EPA should climb toward positive territory as the short-area results and third-down conversion normalize. Expect the 8.7% touchdown rate, which includes five red-zone TDs on 12 plays, to fall back. Expect the 4.3% interception rate to ease, but not below his career-long tendency. That points to 12-15 interceptions over a full season.

Volume is the real question. Seattle is run-leaning by design, but its two primary backs are out and the run game is inefficient. Paired with a top-three defense, that likely means plenty of 25-32 attempt games with occasional shootout spikes. The longer time to throw is worth monitoring behind a line that allows a high hit rate.
swingFactors: Return timeline of Price and Charbonnet and how pass-heavy Seattle gets without them
Whether the 0-9 yard passing game and third-down conversion normalize
Protection holding up with his 3.3-second time to throw

bets.reason: That average is dragged down by a 10%-snap Week 1; his two full games averaged about 274. San Francisco loses Bosa and a DT from a rush that's already 26th in sack rate. Seattle's thin backfield and a 47.5 total point to a passing script.

He has thrown an interception in both full games and ranks 37th in interception rate. He ranked near the bottom in interceptions in each of the last two seasons. A defense that allows few explosives forces tight-window throws, and his aggressiveness is already up to 22%.

The 49ers' offense ranks 1st in EPA. By offensive EPA minus defensive EPA allowed, San Francisco nets out ahead of Seattle, so the home favorite looks shaky. Seattle is 0-1-2 against the spread, including a non-cover as an 8.5-point favorite in Week 3.

confidence.note: Two full games, a conflicting start log and a shifting backfield; career baselines carry most of the weight.
